title: Kuriakose Elias Chavara (3 January)
hookLine: a Syro-Malabar priest in Kerala who started schools for every parish

lines: AND RIGHT BESIDE IT, A SCHOOL.
SOMEONE ASKED FOR IT, ON PURPOSE.
cards: In villages across Kerala, in the south of India, you can still find it: a church, and right next to it, a school. Children in uniforms run between the two at recess.
The school bell and the church bell ring from almost the same spot. It looks so natural that nobody asks why. But that pairing didn't happen on its own.
Someone asked for it, on purpose, parish by parish.

teach.h: A PRIEST OF THE SYRO-MALABAR CHURCH.
teach.b: Kuriakose Elias Chavara was a priest of the Syro-Malabar Church, one of the Eastern Catholic Churches, fully Catholic but with its own liturgy and customs.
Its people trace their faith back, in their tradition, to the apostle Thomas. Chavara grew up in Kerala, was ordained, and gave his life to renewing that Church from the inside.
He helped found a religious congregation of priests and brothers who would pray, preach and teach together. He set up a printing press so books could be made and read at home.
He helped start a congregation of religious sisters too.
And when he was given authority over the Syro-Malabar parishes, he asked that each parish have a school alongside its church, open to the children of the village. Why a school?
For him, faith and learning belonged in the same place. A child who could read could read the Gospels, and also a contract, a letter, a newspaper.
Catholics hear a line of Jesus about children in that work, in the Douay-Rheims: "Suffer the little children, and forbid them not to come to me: for the kingdom of heaven is for such."

Chavara also wrote a letter of advice to families, known as the Testament of a Loving Father, full of plain counsel about raising children, keeping the home peaceful and treating servants and neighbors well.
Pope Francis declared him a saint. His legacy is easy to walk past: a building with desks, next to a building with an altar.

how: Syro-Malabar Catholics in Kerala and around the world honor Saint Kuriakose Elias Chavara in early January, especially at Mannanam, where he is buried, and in the schools and religious communities connected with him.

games.q: you're Chavara, newly given authority over the parishes. you want the faith to grow strong. what do you ask every parish to build?
games.why: he asked for a school alongside each church, open to the village's children. the pairing is still visible across Kerala.

practice: Bring to mind a teacher who changed something for you: the room, the desk, their face, the thing they made possible.
If you pray, pray for them, and for the children in a school near you; if not, simply hold that teacher in mind with gratitude.
